places.name: Thanh Mạch Thôn
places.size: A wheat-farming village of about 220 people: about 45 grey-tile houses gathered round a round polished-stone threshing floor about 30 m across on a hilltop, with green wheat on every side over about 2 km.
places.where: Region 15 (Ngọc Hành Sơn), grassland at 0.51 km on a low rise above a river. On the map: green-gold rolling hills with a river running diagonally to a deep-blue sea at the right, grey rocky crags at the lower right, rust pockets at the left; the sea is a few days away. Held by Thiên Xu Tông; grows the wheat for the mills of Thủy Đối. Nearest: spirit vein Kim Tuệ Mạch (112 km), Chân Kim Các (152 km), town Song Kiều Trấn (160 km). Earth-qi.
places.imagined: Harvest: the heavy stone roller lies on its side on the threshing floor and the whole village sings, and in the fields the last green sheaves fall.
places.subject: The place: Thanh Mạch Thôn, the Green Wheat Village, a farming village on a low hill above a river. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle on a bright early-summer afternoon; green-gold rolling hills fill the frame, a river running diagonally across the lower half toward a deep-blue sea at the right edge, grey rocky crags at the lower right and pockets of rust-red soil at the left. The village: on the crown of a low rounded hill stands a ring of about forty-five houses with grey-tile roofs and whitewashed walls, each with a small yard, a pig-pen, a well and a haystack, packed close around a round threshing floor of polished stone about thirty paces across, its surface pale and worn smooth; a granary on stilts, a tool shed, a cart yard and a long communal hall, with narrow lanes radiating down the slope. Signature element: at the centre of the threshing floor a heavy stone roller stands upright on its end, like a squat pillar, its side grooved, a rope coil at its base; around it the village's meeting place, with small stalls and a stage for festivals; from the hilltop, green wheat falls away on every side in great combed fields, field after field in fresh green, divided by hedgerows and footpaths, with tiny harvesters moving along the lower terraces. Life at scale: a hillside of green wheat and about two hundred small figures. Light: warm gold afternoon light from the upper left, a faint breeze combing the wheat in silver waves, long soft shadows.

places.name: Châu Bạng Thôn
places.size: A pearl-fishing village of about 250 people: about 50 houses whose walls are set all over with oyster shells, a beach of broken shell and about 25 diving boats, spread over about 500 m.
places.where: Region 15 (Ngọc Hành Sơn), grassland at sea level, a port on the inland sea. On the map: green-gold hills with a river reaching a wide deep-blue sea at the right, with a rocky grey ridge and a dark crater to the south. Held by Thiên Xu Tông; pearl oysters gave the village its name in 400 and Tinh Hán Thành its pearl trade. Nearest: peak Quy Bối Sơn (79 km), mine Thạch Hôi Khoáng (90 km), spirit vein Thanh Lưu Mạch (112 km). Water-qi.
places.imagined: Noon: a diver surfaces beside a boat holding up a shell, and the village walls shine white and pearl-grey in the sun like a heap of moons.
places.subject: The place: Châu Bạng Thôn, the Pearl Oyster Village, on the shore of the inland sea. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle at noon; a wide deep-blue sea runs down the right side of the frame with a pale-green band of shallows along its shore, green-gold hills and farm pockets rolling inland on the left with a river entering at the top, a rugged grey ridge at the bottom with a dark round crater, a rocky point at the far right. The village: about fifty houses with grey-tile roofs ranged in a loose crescent along a beach of broken shell, white and cream and silver in the sun; the house walls, from foundation to eaves, are set all over with oyster shells pressed into plaster, so that every wall shines white and pearl-grey with an iridescent shimmer, and from above the whole village looks like a spill of pearls; a long timber pier, a shell-grading hall, a pearl-merchant's inn, rope-and-net lofts, a shrine of stacked shells. Signature element: the shell walls, each house's walls telling how many divers it has raised by the number of embedded first-pearl shells set in its lintel, some houses nearly bare and some thick as armour; about twenty-five diving boats drawn up on the shell beach and others out on the shallows with divers' ropes trailing down and a tiny diver at a boat's edge raising a hand. Life at scale: a small bright working village, the sea glittering around it. Light: strong clean noon light from the upper left, the walls dazzling, the turquoise shallows clear to the bottom.

places.name: Thiên Ngoại Khoáng
places.size: A star-iron mine in a sheer cliff face about 250 m high: about 12 square adits cut in a vertical line with iron chains hanging down to an ore yard, a sorting shed and a stream, with about 150 miners in a few huts.
places.where: Region 15 (Ngọc Hành Sơn), high mountain at 0.69 km. On the map: a huge mass of bare grey and white serrated ridges, two ring-shaped crater peaks at the upper left with snow, a bay of deep-blue sea at the bottom, several small tarns, a river from the right, rust-orange hillside at the right; the sea lies a few days away. Held by Thối Tinh Môn since 335, which says the ore fell with the stars. Nearest: peak Thiết Châm Phong (103 km), mine Thạch Thán Khoáng (112 km), peak Hắc Ưng Phong (125 km). Metal-qi.
places.imagined: A clear afternoon: the chains rattle as ore buckets descend from the adits, and the red face glows against the grey crags.
places.subject: The place: Thiên Ngoại Khoáng, the Mine of the Iron from Beyond the Sky, in a sheer mountain face. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle at mid-afternoon; a huge mass of bare grey and white serrated ridges fills the frame, with two ring-shaped crater rims snowy at the upper left, a bay of deep-blue sea notching in at the bottom, small blue tarns in the hollows, a river curling down at the right and a rust-orange hillside beside it. The mine: on one steep face, streaked rust-red like dried blood, stands a vertical line of about twelve square adits cut one above another, each framed in timber, from which iron chains hang straight down, link by link, to the ore yard at the foot, about two hundred and fifty paces below; on the chains, iron buckets and baskets of dark ore descend and rise; ledges and rope ladders connect the adits; at the bottom, by a clear stream, a long sorting shed with a dark roof, an ore yard with heaped dark lumps and rows of sacks, a mule-line, a small smithy and about a dozen miners' huts. Signature element: the vertical line of adits and the chains hanging like a curtain of black threads down the red face; a tiny cairn shrine to the stars at the foot with offerings. About a hundred and fifty tiny miners, some hanging on ropes. Life at scale: a small bright scar on a huge mountain. Light: bright clear afternoon light from the upper left raking the red face, deep shadows in the clefts, the stream glinting.

places.name: Huyền Thiết Khoáng
places.size: A black-iron mine: one great shaft under a massive stone winch house about 40 m wide, a ramp about 300 m long worn into deep ruts, a smelting and cart yard, about 20 buildings and about 200 miners and oxen-drivers.
places.where: Region 15 (Ngọc Hành Sơn), high mountain at 0.65 km. On the map: bare grey serrated ridges with a dark pit-like ring-peak at the upper left and a snowy crest, a bay of deep-blue sea at the lower left, tarns, rust-orange hills and green forest at the right with a river. Held by Thiên Xu Tông; found in 280, so heavy that a cart carries only one ingot. Nearest: peak Trấn Sơn Phong (75 km), mine Chu Đồng Khoáng (152 km), peak Xích Vũ Phong (160 km). Metal-qi.
places.imagined: A heavy-laden procession: one ox-cart, one black ingot, a driver walking alongside with a long goad, the ramp rutted a hand deep.
places.subject: The place: Huyền Thiết Khoáng, the Black Iron Mine, a deep shaft in a bare mountain. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle at mid-morning; bare grey serrated ridges with a dark ring-peak and a white-snow crest crowd the upper left, a bay of deep-blue sea lies at the lower left, small blue tarns lie in hollows, and at the right rust-orange hills and dark green forest lie by a winding river. The mine: in a narrow mountain valley opens a single great shaft, about thirty paces across, under a massive stone winch house with thick walls, a heavy dark roof and four huge winding drums with iron cables; the shaft mouth is rimmed with black spoil. A broad ramp of beaten earth and stone, about three hundred paces long, runs down to the road, worn by carts into ruts a hand deep and black with dust; below it a yard with squat stone sheds, a forge where ingots are weighed, rows of oxen in stalls, long wooden troughs, and about twenty buildings; the black ingots stacked in a neat cube under guard. Signature element: the line of single ox-carts, about a dozen, each pulled by a very large grey ox, each carrying exactly one black ingot the size of a coffin, descending the ramp one by one with their drivers, slow and heavy; the oxen are visibly the strongest in the mountain. About two hundred tiny miners and drivers. Life at scale: slow, heavy, powerful, dark. Light: bright morning light from the upper left, the black spoil absorbing it, the sea a distant sparkle.

places.name: Can Tương Khoáng
places.size: A sword-ore mine: two adits side by side in grey rock with a small blackened shrine between them, a zigzag path to Phất Y Cốc and about 10 huts; about 60 miners; the whole works about 150 m across on a steep slope.
places.where: Region 15 (Ngọc Hành Sơn), high mountain at 1.0 km. On the map: a steep mass of grey serrated ridges with a dark ring crater at the top, a bay of deep-blue sea at the upper right and green pockets at the lower left; the sea is far below. Held by Phất Y Cốc; named for the swordsmith of legend. Nearest: peak Giới Bi Phong (79 km), peak Huân Yên Phong (103 km), peak Thạch Kính Phong (135 km). Metal-qi.
places.imagined: Two miners carry baskets from the husband and the wife adits and tip them together into one barrow, since a sword of one ore alone will not keep its edge.
places.subject: The place: Can Tương Khoáng, Gan Jiang's Mine, high on a steep slope. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle at early afternoon; a steep mass of grey serrated ridges and gullies fills the frame, with a dark ring-shaped crater at the top, a bay of deep-blue sea glimpsed at the upper right far below, and bright green pockets of grass and low trees at the lower left. The mine: high on a steep slope, two adits open side by side in the grey rock, one a little larger than the other, each framed with stout timber and a stone lintel, with a small stone shrine between them blackened by forge smoke, about the size of a cart, with a tiny bronze bowl; a pair of spoil tips below them, one pale and one reddish, run down the slope and merge into one grey fan; a few sheds, ten rough huts and a charcoal stack; a narrow path zigzags down the slope across the screes toward the valley of the sword sect, with about thirty switchbacks. Signature element: the paired adits, the husband and the wife, and the way the two spoil tips run together; a line of about six tiny miners carrying baskets from both adits to one common barrow at the shrine, where a small pile of two kinds of ore, pale and rust, is mixed; offerings at the shrine, a pair of tiny swords stuck in a stone. Life at scale: a small, devoted, blackened work on an enormous hill. Light: bright clear light from the upper left, deep blue shadows in the gullies, the sea glinting.

places.name: Bạch Ngân Khoáng
places.size: A silver mine: a fan of pale silver-grey spoil spilling from several adit mouths below a cinnabar-red hillside, a walled smelting yard with a squat chimney, about 25 buildings and about 180 miners; the works about 400 m across.
places.where: Region 15 (Ngọc Hành Sơn), high mountain at 0.34 km. On the map: grey serrated ridges with a bay of deep-blue sea at the upper right, a patch of dark green forest and tawny hills with rust-red slope at the lower middle, small tarns; Phượng Minh's border is near. Held by Thiên Xu Tông, whose coin is struck from it; found in 450. Nearest: village Hoàng Hoa Thôn (100 km), spirit vein Lục Nhung Mạch (125 km), peak Quy Vũ Lĩnh (168 km). Metal-qi.
places.imagined: An evening of low light after the war: the slope dipped in two colours, red above and silver below, and the miners walking out of the adits past the silent ridge.
places.subject: The place: Bạch Ngân Khoáng, the Silver Mine, below a hillside stained red with cinnabar. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle in the late afternoon; grey serrated ridges fill the upper half of the frame with a bay of deep-blue sea at the upper right corner, and the lower middle is a patch of dark green forest and tawny hills with a rust-red hillside rising above them, a tiny pond in the grey rock at the left. The mine: below the red slope a fan of pale silver-grey spoil spills out from five adit mouths cut in a line along the foot of the hill, so that the whole slope looks dipped in two colours, vermilion above and silver below, each adit framed in timber with a small iron gate; at the foot, a walled smelting yard with a squat stone chimney, a long assay house, a mint-weighing shed, ore bins, cartways, a mule-line, miners' barracks and about twenty-five buildings, with silver glinting in the stream below. Signature element: the two-coloured slope itself, and a ridge above where, in the Cinnabar Vein War, fighting lit the ridge while the miners slept in the adits; a few old scorch marks on the red hillside and a row of three small stone markers for those lost. About a hundred and eighty tiny miners at the adits and sorting tables. Life at scale: a hard small works under a stained mountain. Light: warm low gold light from the upper left lighting the red slope and the pale fan, long blue shadows from the grey ridges.

places.name: Thanh Ải Phong
places.size: A natural site: the highest peak of Ngọc Hành Sơn, about 3 km high above its surroundings, its upper slopes wrapped in a band of blue haze about 4 km wide that never burns off; at most a few pilgrims' cairns and tiny climbers.
places.where: Region 15 (Ngọc Hành Sơn), high mountain at 3.07 km. On the map: a great mass of bare grey ridges with a white snow crest in the middle, a dark crater at the top right, a tawny-green slope with a river at the left, dark forest and green pockets at the lower right, small tarns; no sea. No sect holds it. Nearest: mine Bạch Kim Khoáng (75 km), peak Hành Vân Phong (79 km), peak Thiên Môn Phong (90 km). Metal-qi.
places.imagined: A morning in which the haze, for once, thins: the summit shows for a moment, and climbers on the paths below stop and look up.
places.subject: The place: Thanh Ải Phong, the Peak of the Blue Haze, the highest peak of Ngọc Hành Sơn. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle on a clear morning; a great mass of bare grey ridges and gullies spreads across the frame, a long white snow crest running through its middle, a dark crater at the upper right, a tawny-green slope with a winding river at the left and dark forest and green pockets at the lower right, a few small tarns. The peak: the highest summit in the picture rises from the middle of the snow crest, about three kilometres above the valley, its upper slopes wrapped in a thick band of soft blue haze, pale periwinkle against the grey, that lies in smooth bands like a scarf and never burns off, so the summit itself is hidden; the haze is wide, about four kilometres across, with a soft upper edge and a clear sharp line where it meets the rock below. Signature element: the haze and, below it, the faint paths of climbers, about thirty tiny figures strung out in thin lines up the ridges, some about to enter the blue; at the haze's edge a small cairn of grey stones, and in the haze one tiny figure half swallowed, its outline pale. No hall, no roofline, though on the very summit, barely visible through a thin patch of haze, the faint shadow of a small temple roof. Life at scale: a peak that dwarfs everything around it. Light: clear gold morning light from the upper left on the snow crest, soft blue shadows, the haze luminous.

places.name: Cùng Mục Phong
places.size: A natural site: a narrow summit of pale granite about 2.6 km high with a flat top rock about 40 m long scored with deep sword cuts, in a field of ranges; a few tiny pilgrims reading the cuts.
places.where: Region 15 (Ngọc Hành Sơn), high mountain at 2.62 km. On the map: a field of bare pale-grey and white-crested ranges with deep blue shadows, a river running down the right side through dark green forest, tarns, a green valley with a stream at the upper left; no sea in view though the plains and the inland sea show from the summit. No sect holds it. Nearest: peak Ngọc Nữ Phong (100 km), mine Xích Ngân Khoáng (141 km), peak Ưng Sào Phong (150 km). Metal-qi.
places.imagined: A clear day with fierce winds: a disciple of the sword sect crouches on the flat top reading the cuts of the three-day duel, one palm laid on a groove.
places.subject: The place: Cùng Mục Phong, the Peak of the Farthest Sight, a narrow pale summit above the ranges. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle on a very clear day; a field of bare pale-grey and white-crested ranges fills the frame in deep blue shadow and bright snow light, a river running down the right side through a band of dark green forest, small tarns in the hollows, a green valley with a stream at the upper left, and a rust patch at the top left. The peak: a narrow summit of pale granite, steep-sided, rising above the neighbouring ranges, so high that its shadow runs far across the lower peaks; on its top a flat rock about forty paces long, wind-scoured and bare, criss-crossed with long, deep sword cuts, dozens of straight white grooves as clean as if cut yesterday, crossing and re-crossing in a pattern of two fighters' footwork. Signature element: the cuts on the summit rock, with, around them, a few tiny pilgrims, about eight, in plain grey, some crouching with a hand on a groove, one lying along a cut to read it, hair and sleeves streaming in the fierce wind; a narrow thread of path, scratched into the granite, climbs from the green valley to the summit with a rope rail near the top, and a small cairn marks where the climbers rest. In the far distance, past the ranges, a hint of plain and a thin silver line of the inland sea. Life at scale: a peak the height of a small mountain range, the figures tiny as seeds. Light: very clear hard gold light from the upper left, long violet shadows across the ranges, the white crests glaring.

places.name: Vạn Trùng Hạp
places.size: A natural site: a deep twisting gorge about 40 km long and 600 m deep, the river racing white between ranks of ridges folded one behind another, with a narrow plank road on beams along one wall; a few boats and walkers.
places.where: Region 15 (Ngọc Hành Sơn), high mountain at 0.67 km on a river. On the map: a river running north-south through a tangle of grey serrated ridges with snow crests, tarns on both sides, tawny-green hills and a rust patch on the left; no sea. No sect holds it. Nearest: ruin Thanh Đăng Tự (100 km), Phất Y Cốc (103 km), mine Lệ Thạch Khoáng (127 km). Earth-qi.
places.imagined: The light boat flies down the white water, the pilot never looking back, while above on the plank road a string of upstream travellers edge along the cliff.
places.subject: The place: Vạn Trùng Hạp, the Gorge of Ten Thousand Mountains, a deep twisting gorge. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle at mid-morning; a river runs top to bottom through the frame in a deep narrow cut, the ranks of ridges on either side folded one behind another like stacked screens, pale grey with white crests on the right and tawny-green hills on the left with a rust-red patch, small blue tarns in the high hollows. The gorge: the river races white between sheer walls, bending in eight tight twists, throwing up foam at every rapid, the water a dark green-blue between the white rapids, and in the deepest bends running in shadow; shelves of fallen rock and small gravel beaches along the foot of the walls; one cliff wall is cut by a narrow plank road on timber beams socketed into the rock, running along it above the rapids for several kilometres, with rope rails and small shelters where the road crosses side gullies. Signature element: the stacked ridges, so many that they look like ten thousand mountains in rank, each paler than the last toward the distance; a single narrow river boat shooting the rapids with a pilot standing at the stern facing forward and a few crew bent over oars; on the plank road a thin line of about twenty tiny travellers with packs and poles going upstream. Life at scale: a river gorge so deep and long that the boat is a seed and the road a thread. Light: gold morning light from the upper left on the western ridges only, the gorge floor in blue shadow, spray glittering.

places.name: Thiết Bối Cốc
places.size: A natural site: a broad highland valley about 20 km across, its rock walls gnawed bare, a herd of about 30 iron-backed beasts each the size of a house; no buildings, at most a hunters' camp of three tents.
places.where: Region 15 (Ngọc Hành Sơn), highland at 1.09 km. On the map: tawny-green rolling highland with dark conifer groves at the upper left, rust-red pockets at the top right and right, a winding river along the bottom, a few small tarns; no sea. No sect holds it. Nearest: hot spring Sa Nhãn Tuyền (180 km), hot spring Bạch Diêm Tuyền (206 km), village Thập Giáp Thôn (224 km). Earth-qi.
places.imagined: Midday: a herd of grey iron-plated shapes moves slowly along a slope, grinding at a vein, while a hunter far below waits for a shed plate.
places.subject: The place: Thiết Bối Cốc, the Iron-Back Valley, a broad highland valley where iron-backed beasts feed on ore. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle at midday; a wide valley of tawny-green rolling highland with dark conifer groves at the upper left, rust-red pockets of bare rock at the upper right, a winding blue river along the lower edge and a few tiny tarns; the valley's rock walls are gnawed and scraped bare in great raw bands, and along the slopes the raw ore shows in bands that gleam like polished metal, silver-grey and dull gold, in long streaks. The beasts: about thirty big grey beasts, each the size of a house, moving slowly among the boulders, their backs plated like iron, a line of overlapping dull grey plates with a metallic sheen, each with a heavy blunt head close to the rock, grinding a vein out with broad jaws; a few small calves follow; scraps of shed plates lie like fallen shields in the grass, glinting. Signature element: the gleaming bands of raw ore on the slopes and the slow grey herd among the boulders; down by the river a hunters' camp of three small tents with a thread of smoke and a pile of collected plates, about eight tiny hunters standing at a respectful distance; one boulder-strewn track shows where a herd on the move flattened an old camp. Life at scale: slow, heavy, mostly calm. Light: bright midday light from the upper left, the ore bands gleaming, short soft shadows.

places.name: Xích Viêm Khẩu
places.size: A natural site: a bare black cone about 1.5 km across and 300 m high with a wide red mouth about 150 m across, ringed by about 12 carved grey warding pillars on the lower slope; at most a smith's camp for a single working.
places.where: Region 15 (Ngọc Hành Sơn), volcano at 1.2 km. On the map: a dark ring-shaped cone on a ridge of bare grey rock running down to a bay of deep-blue sea, green-gold highland and a stream at the upper left, small forest pockets at the lower right. Held by Thiên Xu Tông; a vent of the volcano of Ngọc Hành Sơn. Nearest: ruin Tuần Hải Bảo (79 km), ruin Thủ Hỏa Bảo (90 km), peak Huân Yên Phong (112 km). Fire-qi.
places.imagined: Dusk: the vent breathes red and its lava cools with a metallic sheen while a smith and an alchemist draw fire for a single working before they leave.
places.subject: The place: Xích Viêm Khẩu, the Red Flame Mouth, a vent of the mountain's volcano. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle at dusk; a bare ridge of grey serrated rock runs diagonally down the frame to the shore of a bay of deep-blue sea at the right, green-gold highland with a stream winding through it at the upper left, small pockets of dark forest at the lower right and a low violet sky. The vent: on the ridge stands a bare black cone about fifteen hundred paces across, steep-sided and ash-black with streaks of rust and grey; at its summit a wide red mouth about one hundred and fifty paces across glows orange and crimson and breathes heat in a visible shimmer, with a thin plume of grey-white fumes; a tongue of lava has run down one flank and cooled into a black river with a metallic blue-grey and gold sheen, its far end still red. Signature element: on the lower slope a ring of about twelve carved grey warding pillars, each the height of a house and carved with spiralling lines, stands in a perfect circle around the cone, glowing faintly pale-blue where they meet the heat, with an empty ground inside; outside the ring, on the ridge, a small camp of one tent with two tiny figures, a smith and an alchemist in grey, waiting to draw fire for a single working; a horse and a cart of iron vessels. Life at scale: a huge, dangerous quiet, the red glow reflected in the sea. Light: deep violet dusk with a last gold on the ridge from the upper left, the red vent the brightest point, its glow on the nearby rock.

places.name: Chân Kim Các
places.size: A minor sect of about 40 assayers, refiners and clerks: a walled settlement of about 35 buildings about 200 m across on a forested hill edge, with assay halls and a standard-weights vault.
places.where: Region 15 (Ngọc Hành Sơn), temperate forest at 0.43 km, five tiles above Song Kiều. On the map: bright green grassland hills with a river running diagonally and dark conifer groves, a jagged grey crag at the lower middle, a turquoise bay of the sea at the right edge, rust patch at the lower left. Vassal of Thiên Xu Tông, neutral. Earth 32 %, metal 23 %, fire 20 %. Nearest: mine Thanh Thiết Khoáng (125 km), town Song Kiều Trấn (127 km), village Thanh Mạch Thôn (152 km). Earth-qi.
places.imagined: Morning: an assayer in grey drops a test-stone on the touchstone, a clerk writes the result, and across the court a refiner holds a bar of gold up to the sun.
places.subject: The place: Chân Kim Các, the Pavilion of True Gold, a small assay sect at a forest edge. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle on a bright morning; bright green grassland hills fill the frame, a clear river winding diagonally across it with a branch joining, dark conifer groves on the knolls, a jagged grey crag at the lower middle, a rust-orange patch at the lower left and, at the right edge, a turquoise bay of the sea with a pale surf line. The sect: about thirty-five buildings of grey stone and dark tile at the edge of a pine wood on a hill, inside a low wall of squared stone, arranged in two courts: the front court of long assay halls with high skylit roofs and rows of benches, scales and touchstones on tables; a vault of thick stone with an iron door where standard weights and sample bars are kept; refining sheds with squat furnaces and small chimneys; a clerks' hall with long rows of desks; a small guest house, a kitchen and a few dwellings. Signature element: in the front court, forty tiny assayers and clerks work at long tables in the open air under white awnings, each table with a balance and a touchstone, and rows of gold, silver and copper bars laid out in order of purity from pale to deep colour, glinting in the sun like a spectrum; a standard measure post stands in the court's centre with notches. Life at scale: a quiet, exact, spotless little place. Light: clear gold morning light from the upper left, the bars gleaming, short crisp shadows of the awnings.
